content.text:
**Bun** is a fast all-in-one JavaScript/TypeScript runtime, bundler, and package manager built on Apple's **JavaScriptCore** engine (instead of V8 like Node.js) with its core written in Rust (as of Bun 1.4, following a major rewrite from Zig). It emphasizes low startup time, high throughput, low memory usage, and strong performance in real-world workloads.[[1]](https://bun.com/docs/runtime)

### Startup Time
Bun consistently shows significantly faster startup than Node.js:
- On Linux: A simple `hello.js` starts in **~5.1–5.2 ms** with Bun 1.4 vs. **~25–27 ms** for Node.js (roughly **4–5x faster**).[[2]](https://bun.com/docs/project/benchmarking)
- On Windows: **~15.5 ms** for Bun 1.4 vs. **~40 ms** for Node.js (~2.5x faster).[[3]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- `bun run` (or `bun <script>`) for npm scripts is dramatically faster: ~**6–7 ms** vs. 130–260 ms for yarn/pnpm/npm.[[4]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.0)

Bun 1.4 improved startup by ~50% on Linux and 2.5x on Windows compared to 1.3.[[5]](https://daily.dev/posts/bun-1-4-nz2dmgftt)

### Runtime & Memory Efficiency (Bun 1.4)
The Rust rewrite brought major gains:
- **Idle CPU usage** reduced by up to **5x**.
- **Memory usage** for HTTP servers cut by **13–48%** (e.g., Fastify: 233 MB → 120 MB; Express: 169 MB → 92 MB; Next.js: 397 MB → 285 MB).[[3]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- Real-world production deployments (e.g., at Scrydon) saw ~50% lower average CPU and ~60% lower memory across services.[[6]](https://scrydon.com/insights/2026/08/21/bun-1-4-at-scrydon/)

The `--smol` flag further reduces memory (at some performance cost) for constrained environments.[[1]](https://bun.com/docs/runtime)

### HTTP & Server Performance
Bun's `Bun.serve()` (and frameworks like Elysia/Hono built on it) excels in many scenarios:
- **Express over HTTPS**: ~**48k req/s** (Bun 1.4) vs. ~25k (Node.js 26) and ~19k (Deno), with lower peak RAM (~105 MB vs. 142–176 MB).[[7]](https://r.jina.ai/https:/bun.com/)
- In mixed workloads (JSON, compression, static files, DB queries), Bun ranked **#1** in some independent tests (e.g., HttpArena), beating even some Rust servers in efficiency while using far less memory.[[8]](https://dev.to/fbio_reis_355b87b508598e/bun-http-server-1-in-mixed-workloads-41-in-pipelining-the-full-picture-httparena-deep-dive-4h6e)
- Strong in JSON serialization, compression, and database queries (e.g., Postgres: ~20k queries/s vs. ~10k for Node/Deno).[[7]](https://r.jina.ai/https:/bun.com/)
- WebSocket performance is excellent (millions of messages/sec in some cases).[[7]](https://r.jina.ai/https:/bun.com/)

However, performance is **workload-dependent**:
- One analysis of Next.js workloads showed Bun with notably higher average latency (~246 ms) and worse tail latency (p99 ~974 ms) compared to Node.js (~20 ms) or Deno (~11–14 ms), despite handling the load.[[9]](https://blog.platformatic.dev/bun-is-fast-until-latency-matters-for-nextjs-workloads)
- It ranked lower in pipelining or certain upload scenarios.[[8]](https://dev.to/fbio_reis_355b87b508598e/bun-http-server-1-in-mixed-workloads-41-in-pipelining-the-full-picture-httparena-deep-dive-4h6e)

### Other Benchmarks
- **Bundling/Builds**: Bun's bundler is often 1.75x faster than esbuild and dramatically faster than Webpack/Rollup/Parcel. Real-world builds (e.g., Next.js apps) can be 1.8–2x faster; package installs up to 3–8x faster.[[4]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.0)
- **Testing**: `bun test` is often 8–13x faster than Jest/Vitest.[[4]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.0)
- **FFI & Streams**: Bun 1.4 made FFI up to ~3–4x faster and improved native streams significantly (e.g., much higher throughput and lower memory for Compression/Text streams).[[5]](https://daily.dev/posts/bun-1-4-nz2dmgftt)

### Summary
Bun 1.4 (current major version as of 2026) delivers excellent **startup speed**, **memory efficiency**, and **throughput** for many server, scripting, and build workloads—often outperforming Node.js and Deno in raw speed and resource usage. It shines in mixed/realistic apps and has seen big compatibility/stability improvements. That said, results vary by workload (e.g., some latency-sensitive or specific I/O patterns may favor alternatives), so benchmarking your specific use case is recommended. Official benchmarks and tools like `mitata`, `hyperfine`, or `bombardier` are available in the Bun docs.[[2]](https://bun.com/docs/project/benchmarking)

For the latest numbers, check the official Bun blog, docs, or independent tests, as performance continues to evolve rapidly.
